amendments.because: A fixed size and every round's own summary forever cannot both hold; the owner's goal is never hitting the limit
amendments.done_when: The pull request keeps per-round time summaries rather than every event, so a long item never reaches the body limit and keeps its whole round history

done_when: The pull request time record has a fixed size limit: it keeps a time summary for each of the recent rounds and folds older rounds into one totals line, so a long item never reaches the body limit and the board still shows its total time

findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 3, Harm 4
Raise: Not done
Once more than 16 earlier rounds have been summarised, `_fold` replaces the oldest two round records with one aggregate `Rounds 1–N` record. Their individual time summaries are no longer in the pull request, so a fresh clone cannot recover how long any one of those rounds took. The 200-round case exercises this loss; it treats the aggregate range as if it retained each round.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Scale
The saved `state.review` added at `time_records.py:373` has neither `round` nor `at`, so `_settled` never removes it from this `clean_reviews` list. Repeated clean reviews after changes or failed checks therefore retain full prior review results, including findings, indefinitely. When the body fills, `_bounded_body` removes current event and timing rows before these snapshots (`close.py:920`), losing the current time record the fix promises to keep.
findings.title: Clean review snapshots still grow without bound

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
The test expands a `Rounds 1–N` aggregate into a list of round numbers, then checks only the aggregate reviewing total. It passes while the implementation discards the individual time summaries for older rounds. The named proof therefore cannot fail when the Done-when requirement to keep per-round time history breaks.
